results.name: single_example_nonmember_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets on single-example sets; observed > model means people generalize more broadly from one example than the model's size-principle posterior (with n**gamma evidence weighting) predicts, observed < model means more conservative.
results.code:
# name: single_example_nonmember_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets on single-example sets; observed > model means people generalize more broadly from one example than the model's size-principle posterior (with n**gamma evidence weighting) predicts, observed < model means more conservative.
def test_statistic(df):
    u = pd.Series(df["number_set"].astype(str).unique())
    parsed = {s: [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = ns.map(lambda s: len(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    lo = ns.map(lambda s: min(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    hi = ns.map(lambda s: max(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    first = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][0]).to_numpy()
    last = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][-1]).to_numpy()
    member = np.array([tt in parsed[s] for s, tt in zip(ns.to_numpy(), t)])
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    return rate((n == 1) & ~member)

results.name: intermediate_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of (set,target) cells with >=4 responses whose observed yes-proportion lies strictly between 0.25 and 0.75; observed > model means responses are more graded/inconsistent across trials than the model's near-deterministic concept posterior predicts, observed < model means more all-or-none.

def test_statistic(df):
    u = pd.Series(df["number_set"].astype(str).unique())
    parsed = {s: [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = ns.map(lambda s: len(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    lo = ns.map(lambda s: min(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    hi = ns.map(lambda s: max(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    first = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][0]).to_numpy()
    last = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][-1]).to_numpy()
    member = np.array([tt in parsed[s] for s, tt in zip(ns.to_numpy(), t)])
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    g = pd.DataFrame({"c": ns.to_numpy() + "|" + pd.Series(t).astype(str).to_numpy(), "y": y})
    agg = g.groupby("c")["y"].agg(["mean", "size"])
    agg = agg[agg["size"] >= 4]
    if len(agg) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(((agg["mean"] > 0.25) & (agg["mean"] < 0.75)).mean())

results.name: wide_range_inside_hull_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets inside the [min,max] range of multi-example sets whose range spans >=40; observed < model means people do not fill wide example ranges as an interval (they treat spread examples as a rule/sparse set), observed > model means more interval-filling than predicted.

def test_statistic(df):
    u = pd.Series(df["number_set"].astype(str).unique())
    parsed = {s: [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = ns.map(lambda s: len(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    lo = ns.map(lambda s: min(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    hi = ns.map(lambda s: max(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    first = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][0]).to_numpy()
    last = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][-1]).to_numpy()
    member = np.array([tt in parsed[s] for s, tt in zip(ns.to_numpy(), t)])
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0

results.name: above_minus_below_hull_asymmetry
results.description: Among targets 1-20 units outside the example range (any set size), yes-rate for targets above the max minus yes-rate for targets below the min; observed > model means people extend upward (larger numbers) more than the symmetric-in-linear-space model predicts, observed < model means downward extension is under-predicted.

def test_statistic(df):
    u = pd.Series(df["number_set"].astype(str).unique())
    parsed = {s: [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = ns.map(lambda s: len(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    lo = ns.map(lambda s: min(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    hi = ns.map(lambda s: max(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    first = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][0]).to_numpy()
    last = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][-1]).to_numpy()
    member = np.array([tt in parsed[s] for s, tt in zip(ns.to_numpy(), t)])
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    above = (t > hi) & (t - hi <= 20)
    below = (t < lo) & (lo - t <= 20)
    return rate(above) - rate(below)

results.name: shared_last_digit_boost_outside_hull
results.description: Among targets outside the example range (excluding examples), yes-rate for targets sharing a last digit with some example minus yes-rate for those that do not; observed > model means surface digit similarity drives generalization more than the model's ends-in-d rules capture.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_boost_outside_hull
# description: Among targets outside the example range (excluding examples), yes-rate for targets sharing a last digit with some example minus yes-rate for those that do not; observed > model means surface digit similarity drives generalization more than the model's ends-in-d rules capture.
def test_statistic(df):
    u = pd.Series(df["number_set"].astype(str).unique())
    parsed = {s: [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = ns.map(lambda s: len(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    lo = ns.map(lambda s: min(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    hi = ns.map(lambda s: max(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    first = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][0]).to_numpy()
    last = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][-1]).to_numpy()
    member = np.array([tt in parsed[s] for s, tt in zip(ns.to_numpy(), t)])
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    nsa = ns.to_numpy()
    shares = np.array([(tt % 10) in {x % 10 for x in parsed[s]} for s, tt in zip(nsa, t)])
    out = ((t < lo) | (t > hi)) & ~member
    return rate(out & shares) - rate(out & ~shares)

results.name: late_minus_early_inside_hull
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets inside the example range on late trials (trial_index>=300) minus early trials (trial_index<150), multi-example sets only; the model attributes session drift to blind-yes mainly on excluded targets, so observed far from model means in-range acceptance changes over the session differently (observed < model: in-range yes falls or stays flat late).
results.code:
# name: late_minus_early_inside_hull
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets inside the example range on late trials (trial_index>=300) minus early trials (trial_index<150), multi-example sets only; the model attributes session drift to blind-yes mainly on excluded targets, so observed far from model means in-range acceptance changes over the session differently (observed < model: in-range yes falls or stays flat late).
def test_statistic(df):
    u = pd.Series(df["number_set"].astype(str).unique())
    parsed = {s: [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = ns.map(lambda s: len(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    lo = ns.map(lambda s: min(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    hi = ns.map(lambda s: max(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    first = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][0]).to_numpy()
    last = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][-1]).to_numpy()
    member = np.array([tt in parsed[s] for s, tt in zip(ns.to_numpy(), t)])
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    tr = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    m = (n >= 2) & ~member & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    return rate(m & (tr >= 300)) - rate(m & (tr < 150))

results.name: near_outside_hull_yes_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets 1-10 units outside the [min,max] range of multi-example sets; observed > model means people generalize past the example range by similarity more than the model's hard interval/rule concepts allow (observed < model: sharper edges).
results.code:
# name: near_outside_hull_yes_rate
# description: Yes-rate for targets 1-10 units outside the [min,max] range of multi-example sets; observed > model means people generalize past the example range by similarity more than the model's hard interval/rule concepts allow (observed < model: sharper edges).
def test_statistic(df):
    u = pd.Series(df["number_set"].astype(str).unique())
    parsed = {s: [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = ns.map(lambda s: len(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    lo = ns.map(lambda s: min(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    hi = ns.map(lambda s: max(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    first = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][0]).to_numpy()
    last = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][-1]).to_numpy()
    member = np.array([tt in parsed[s] for s, tt in zip(ns.to_numpy(), t)])
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    d = np.maximum(lo - t, t - hi)
    m = (n >= 2) & (d >= 1) & (d <= 10)
    return rate(m)

results.name: last_vs_first_example_proximity
results.description: Among non-member targets of multi-example sets whose first and last shown examples differ by >=10, yes-rate for targets strictly closer to the last-shown example minus yes-rate for targets strictly closer to the first-shown example; observed > model means a recency/order effect the order-blind model under-produces (observed < model means primacy).
results.code:
# name: last_vs_first_example_proximity
# description: Among non-member targets of multi-example sets whose first and last shown examples differ by >=10, yes-rate for targets strictly closer to the last-shown example minus yes-rate for targets strictly closer to the first-shown example; observed > model means a recency/order effect the order-blind model under-produces (observed < model means primacy).
def test_statistic(df):
    u = pd.Series(df["number_set"].astype(str).unique())
    parsed = {s: [int(x) for x in s.split(",")] for s in u}
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = ns.map(lambda s: len(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    lo = ns.map(lambda s: min(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    hi = ns.map(lambda s: max(parsed[s])).to_numpy()
    first = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][0]).to_numpy()
    last = ns.map(lambda s: parsed[s][-1]).to_numpy()
    member = np.array([tt in parsed[s] for s, tt in zip(ns.to_numpy(), t)])
    def rate(m):
        return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    m = (n >= 2) & ~member & (np.abs(last - first) >= 10)
    dl = np.abs(t - last); dfst = np.abs(t - first)
    return rate(m & (dl < dfst)) - rate(m & (dfst < dl))
